decisions.reason: As a standard rye bread in a German bakery portfolio, it likely has low carrying cost and too little negative evidence after one year to justify abandoning the option.
The repeated gold medal is strong positive information that reduces uncertainty and supports continued commitment to this seasonal premium stollen.
A seeded rye mixed bread fits established German demand and can be kept on the market cheaply while management learns more about its longer-run sales potential.
Its darker malt-rye positioning is somewhat more niche, but with no clear failure signal yet the firm would usually preserve the option for another period.
The marzipan stollen faces more overlap with the stronger raisin premium stollen, but as a seasonal product its option value can still outweigh the limited cost of keeping it for another season.
As a newly introduced ancient-grain specialty bread, uncertainty about demand is still resolving and the differentiated concept gives management reason to keep the option open.
